title: Case: Shipper writes again about a parcel of home-baked biscuits on its way back from abroad
context: Hesper Ingleby posted home-baked ginger biscuits to her son abroad on DL-9256 from the Foxhallow Arc parcel counter at Quillmoor Lane on 2 March. The parcel was refused at destination and is returning.
initial_request: No. Thought about it. Baked 28 Feb. More than three weeks in a box. They are bad now. Do not send again. Not paying twice to post bad biscuits. Want the postage back. Is not much money. But was your counter not me. Three people three answers. I did what the last one said. Gave the list. Sons birthday was the 9th. Dont want the box back either really. What happens now.

acceptable_actions.summary: Tell them the shipper has withdrawn the re-send, ask them to lift the re-ship hold before 24 March, and pass on her request for a postage review and a decision on the returning box.

must: Tells Delivery investigations by Email that the shipper has withdrawn the re-send request and asks them to remove the re-ship hold on DL-9256 before the parcel reaches Quillmoor Lane on 24 March
Passes on her request for a review of the original postage as a request for their decision, under DI-2341
Says she does not want the box returned to her and asks what the disposition will be
Tells the team she was given conflicting answers at the counter and supplied the ingredients list as the last one asked, so they can weigh that in the postage review
must_not: Leaves the re-ship standing, confirms the parcel will be sent again, or passes on a re-ship quote
Promises or implies the postage will be refunded
Tells the shipper that food is sent at the sender's risk or that no refund is possible
States that the biscuits are spoiled, or that they are still fine to eat, as the desk's own judgement
Tells the shipper the box will be destroyed or returned before Delivery investigations decides
Treats label-scan-878.txt as evidence about DL-9256: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-58320)
Tells anyone that DL-9256 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-878.txt
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DI-2341 / DL-9256. The shipper, Hesper Ingleby, has withdrawn her request to send the parcel again. Please remove the re-ship hold before it reaches Quillmoor Lane on 24 March and do not quote re-ship postage. Her reason: the biscuits were baked on 28 February and she will not pay to post them a second time. She asks for the original postage to be reviewed, and says she does not want the box back; please tell me what the disposition will be. For your review: the counter note of 2 March records that she was told no food, then to try, then that food could go with an ingredients list; she supplied the list, it was scanned, and it did not travel with the consignment. The parcel was for her son's birthday on 9 March. I have promised her nothing on the postage.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2603: people, organisations and references renamed. label-scan-878.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-58320); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. 41 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
